text: Imagine opening your eyes… and the year is 80 AD.
You are standing in a narrow street in Rome. The Sun is not even up yet.
But the street is already full. Thousands of people, all walking in the same direction.
Not to the market. Not to the temple.
To the largest building the Roman world has ever seen.
The Flavian Amphitheatre. Today, we call it the Colosseum.
Forty-eight metres high. Built in about ten years. Room for around fifty thousand people.
At ground level it has eighty arches. Seventy-six of them are numbered, so every visitor can find the way to their seat.
Someone presses a small clay token into your hand. Gate twenty-three.
Today, the emperor Titus opens the games. They will go on for one hundred days.
Fifty thousand voices, inside a single ring of stone.
And once the games begin… there is no easy way out.
